claims.text: All three load-bearing artifacts describe the same trip: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown each carry trip_id TRP-00515, and the timestamps cohere (accepted 17:30:40, started 17:36:40, first GPS fix 17:36:40, ended/last fix 18:37:40). The rider's threshold case under POL-RD-08(a) is therefore made out, and the booked optimal route on the trip record is 34.2 km and 40.0 minutes.

The governing distance is the trace figure, not the rounded trip-record copy. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km (48.82 km) govern where it disagrees with trip_record.actual_distance_km (48.8 km), and the trip-record field may not be cited for the threshold test. Measured on the governing figure against the 34.2 km optimal, the excess is 14.62 km.

The deviation is established on both limbs of POL-RD-01: an excess of 14.62 km is more than 20% of the 34.2 km optimal (the 20% line is 6.84 km) and more than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The trace reports the excess as 42.75% of optimal.
The deviation is additionally MATERIAL: an excess of 14.62 km exceeds the 8.0 km absolute materiality threshold set out in POL-RD-01, which in turn requires the driver_profile check under POL-RD-06.

The trace is clean for policy purposes. It carries 367 fixes at a 10 s interval against an expected 10 s, no gaps at all, max_gap_sec 0.0 and 100% coverage. It meets none of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07, so no impairment discount applies, the measured excess is the excess, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged.

The driver has no admissible exculpation. His statement blames a confusing KPE split and an admission that he missed it, but he cites no advisory. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00515-01, is MISSING: status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. POL-RD-03 cannot be run without a named corridor and validity window, and under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 the assertion carries no weight; the measured excess therefore stands unreduced.

There was no rider-requested detour. The chat log holds exactly one message, the rider asking the driver to put the phone down, with waypoint_hint null and no road or place named. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction that identifies a waypoint or road and is corroborated by the vehicle passing within 200 m of it; neither exists here, so the clause is unavailable to the driver and no part of the excess is excluded.

The optimal baseline is the booked optimal of 34.2 km. This trip is RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline and its co-rider exclusion do not apply and cannot be used to explain any part of the 14.62 km excess away.

A repeat deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3, which meets the clause's threshold of 3 or more, against 180 completed trips in the same window (well above the 40-trip floor). Under POL-GEN-01 the claim rests on those two named fields only and on no other profile field.

Because the POL-RD-06 pattern is established, and because this deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own trace, limb (b) uplifts the remedy from the POL-RD-02 partial to FULL_REFUND of charged_total. The two figures printed side by side, as the clause requires: POL-RD-02 standing alone yields SGD 20.85 (charged_total 62.28 less recomputed_fare 41.45, rounded up); the uplifted outcome is the entire charged_total of SGD 62.28 — SGD 58.28 of distance, time and platform charges uplifted by this limb, plus the SGD 4.00 of off-route ERP which POL-RD-09 settles on its own footing and which this limb does not need to uplift.

If the uplift is declined, the ordinary POL-RD-02 arithmetic still runs: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 34.2 + 0.28 x 40.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP on the optimal route = 41.45; refund = 62.28 - 41.45 = 20.83, rounded up to SGD 20.85 payable. The fare_model is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE, so POL-RD-02 and not POL-RD-11 governs, and the surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is 1.0.

The SGD 4.00 of ERP is wholly off-route: both charged gantries, TPE (Seletar Link towards Punggol) and TPE (Punggol Rd towards Tampines), carry on_optimal_route = false, and each is matched to a trace fix at 0 m. Under POL-RD-09 these pass-through lines travel with the deviation refund, are itemised separately in the ruling, and are never added on top of the distance-and-time figure a second time.

The rider's account is corroborated beyond the trace, so the case is not a trace-only case. At 17:48:40, twelve minutes into the trip, the rider messaged 'can you please put the phone down and drive', and the driver's own counter-statement concedes 'I was checking the navigation on my phone'. That combination supports the POL-RD-06(c) referral to driver-conduct review, which is recorded in the ruling's referrals list and does not displace or delay the monetary outcome.

The rider carries no adverse claim history that would add a corroboration burden. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 rider-side trigger (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) does not fire, and the ordinary burden is discharged on this trip's own trace. Under POL-GEN-01 no other rider profile field bears on the outcome.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance figure is the trace, gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 48.82 km, not the rounded trip_record convenience copy of 48.8 km. Measured against the 34.2 km booked optimal, the excess is 14.62 km, or 42.75 percent. That is the whole of the departure the rider can point to: 34.2 of the 48.8 km driven was the optimal route, so a claim to the entire 62.28 SGD fare is not supported by this trip's own measurement.

The rider's account of a driver 'driving slowly so he could keep scrolling' is contradicted by the driver's own trace: 367 fixes at a 10 s cadence record sustained speeds clustered in the 45-50 kph band with a single low reading of 4.4 kph, and the trace carries no hard-braking or lane-drift signature at all. The narrative, not the data, is doing the work in that part of the claim.

The trip ran 61 minutes against a 40-minute optimal - 21 minutes over, not the 'forty minutes became ninety' of the claim - and the only in-app message on the trip is the rider's own, sent at 17:48:40. Under POL-RD-02 the recomputation runs on optimal_duration_min = 40.0 against the recording engine's duration, not against the rider's account of the journey.

The substance of the claim - phone use, two hard brakes, lane drift and the rider's fear - is a conduct complaint. No line of the fare_breakdown prices conduct, and the route-deviation policy's only monetary remedy is the arithmetic recomputation in POL-RD-02. Under POL-GEN-03 the ruling moves the figure that arithmetic produces for a route deviation and nothing more; conduct is a referral matter, not a fare line.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 367 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100 percent coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is therefore not engaged, the trace is not impaired for policy purposes, and there is no POL-RD-10(3) escalation available on this bundle.

Both charged ERP gantries carry a trace fix at 0 m - well inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 uses - so both gantries were crossed by this vehicle. Neither line is a phantom crossing: there is no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding to record and no POL-RD-10(8) escalation on this bundle.

The 4.00 SGD of off-route ERP is already comprehended in the fare refund under POL-RD-09(1) and must never be added on top of it. The driver's exposure on this trip is one figure, not a sum made of a distance refund plus the gantry lines itemised a second time.

The meter was not inflated. The distance charged, 48.8 km, matches the 48.82 km the trace records, and the time charged, 61.0 minutes, matches the trip record; the fare model on this trip is METERED, so the billed lines are the trace lines. The driver billed no more distance or time than the trace shows he drove, so the rider is not paying for padded meter movement.

Any POL-RD-06 pattern finding must rest on driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d alone: POL-GEN-01 makes prior_deviation_flags - 5 on this profile - a lifetime counter that is context only and cannot be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure the clause names, and the trailing-window rate here is 3 of 180 trips, 1.67 percent, far below the clause's 5 percent limb. Any uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is an uplift on the remedy, not on the finding, and it does not touch the government and third-party pass-through lines, which are settled once under POL-RD-09.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is one trip, TRP-00515, Blk 342 Jurong East St 31 to Blk 612 Punggol Dr on 3 Sep 2026. The ruling is FULL_REFUND — the whole charged fare of SGD 62.28 is returned to the rider.

Why the deviation is established. The booked optimal route is 34.2 km / 40.0 min. For the distance test POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure, and gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 48.82 km; the 48.8 km on the trip record is a rounded convenience copy and may not be cited for the threshold. The excess is 14.62 km, or 42.75% of optimal — over both the 20% and 0.8 km establishment tests, so a deviation is ESTABLISHED. The same excess exceeds the 8.0 km absolute materiality threshold, so it is additionally MATERIAL.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 367 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps, max gap 0 s, 100% coverage. It meets none of POL-RD-07(a)–(c), so nothing is impaired and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises. Both charged gantries are matched to trace fixes at 0 m, so no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity issue arises either.

No excuse reduces the excess. The driver's explanation (the KPE split is confusing, he missed it) is a traffic-cause assertion with no advisory behind it. The bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-00515-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run; under POL-RD-08 the uncited assertion carries no weight, and under POL-RD-13 a missing advisory no party cited is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) trigger. There was no rider-requested detour (the single chat message names no waypoint, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot run) and no pickup/dropoff amendment (POL-RD-05 does not apply). The vehicle is RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply, and the fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply.

The POL-RD-02 arithmetic. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 × 34.2 km + 0.28 × 40.0 min) × 1.0 surge (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP on the optimal route = SGD 41.45. Refund = 62.28 − 41.45 = 20.83, rounded up to SGD 20.85. That is the ordinary deviation refund.

Why the ruling is more than that. POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, so POL-RD-06 required the driver_profile check. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3 against completed_trips_90d of 180; the clause is met at '3 or more', so a repeat deviation pattern is ESTABLISHED. The driver's point that the rate is only 1.67% and so below the 5% limb fails, because the clause is disjunctive and the '3 or more' limb already fires; the driver's other point — that the uplift does not touch the government/third-party pass-through lines — is correct and is applied. Because a pattern is established and the deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own trace, POL-RD-06(b) uplifts the remedy. Side by side, as the clause requires: POL-RD-02 alone yields SGD 20.85; the uplifted figure is the full charged_total of SGD 62.28.

The ERP. Both gantries, TPE (Seletar Link towards Punggol) and TPE (Punggol Rd towards Tampines), are off the optimal route and total SGD 4.00. Under POL-RD-09(1) these pass-through lines are comprehended in the deviation refund and are never added on top a second time; they are itemised here for transparency only. The 62.28 therefore comprises SGD 58.28 of distance, time and platform charges plus SGD 4.00 of off-route ERP, settled once.

What is not accepted. The rider's account that 'forty minutes became ninety' is not supported — the trip ran 61 minutes against a 40-minute optimal. The account of the driver crawling while scrolling is not supported either — the trace shows sustained speeds in the 45–50 kph band. No fare line prices phone use, hard braking or fear, and under POL-GEN-03 the ruling moves only the route-deviation figure; the conduct is dealt with by the referral, not by a fare line. The driver's claim that the rider is not entitled to the whole fare is right under POL-RD-02 alone but is outweighed by the POL-RD-06(b) uplift. The driver's remaining claims — trace unimpaired, both ERP lines genuine crossings, meter not inflated — are accepted and reflected above. driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was not used for any finding.

Referral. Because the pattern is established, POL-RD-06(c) requires a referral to driver-conduct review. It rides with this ruling and does not delay the refund.

Confidence: 0.90. Every artifact this ruling rests on — trip record, GPS trace, fare breakdown and driver profile — carries weight 1.0, so the cap on confidence is 1.0.
referrals: POL-RD-06(c): refer driver DRV-21377 to driver-conduct review — a repeat deviation pattern is established (deviation_flags_90d = 3 against completed_trips_90d = 180), which requires the referral independently of the monetary outcome.

This referral does not displace or delay the monetary ruling.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver.

ROUTE. The GPS trace governs the distance and records 48.82 km driven on TRP-00515 against the booked optimal of 34.2 km — an excess of 14.62 km, 42.75% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED, and because it also exceeds 8.0 km it is additionally MATERIAL. The trace is clean for policy purposes — 367 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, 100% coverage — so POL-RD-07 is not engaged and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises. The rider's 'forty minutes became ninety' is not borne out: the trip ran 61 minutes against a 40-minute optimal.

EXCULPATION. None applies. The only chat message is the rider's own and carries waypoint_hint null, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run and excludes nothing. The driver's statement that the KPE split was confusing finds no support: the bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00515-01, is MISSING (status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), and no party cited an advisory ID, so under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 the assertion carries no weight and the measured excess stands unreduced.

The driver's argument that no POL-RD-06 pattern can be established is NOT accepted. POL-RD-06 is met by either limb, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3, which alone establishes the pattern against 180 completed trips in the same window (well above the 40-trip floor). The 1.67% rate argument addresses only the second limb. POL-GEN-01 is respected — only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d are used; prior_deviation_flags (5) is a lifetime counter and is context only, as the driver correctly says.

MONEY. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs on the fare_breakdown. Read from that artifact: charged_total 62.28; recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 34.2 + 0.28 x 40.0) x surge 1.0 (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP on the optimal route = 41.45. POL-RD-02 refund = 62.28 - 41.45 = 20.83, rounded up to SGD 20.85. Standing alone that would be a PARTIAL_REFUND, and that is the figure the driver's arithmetic claim reaches.

POL-RD-06(b) UPLIFT. Because the pattern is established and this deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own trace, limb (b) uplifts the remedy to FULL_REFUND of charged_total. The two figures side by side, as the clause requires: POL-RD-02 standing alone, SGD 20.85; uplifted, SGD 62.28. The distance, time, base and platform lines (SGD 58.28) are uplifted by this limb. The SGD 4.00 of ERP is NOT uplifted but is settled under POL-RD-09 — both charged gantries carry on_optimal_route = false and are matched to trace fixes at 0 m, so they are refunded as off-route pass-through and are never added on top of the distance figure a second time (POL-RD-09(1)). The meter itself was not padded: distance charged 48.8 km matches the trace's 48.82 km and time charged 61.0 minutes matches the trip record.

CONDUCT. The rider's account of phone use, hard braking and lane drift prices no fare line under this policy, so it does not move the money directly — and the trace shows sustained running in the 45-50 kph band with no braking or drift signature. It does produce a referral: under POL-RD-06(c) the driver goes to driver-conduct review, which rides with the money and does not delay it. Both gantry lines are genuine crossings, so there is no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding and no referral on that ground.

CONFIDENCE 0.90. Every fact the ruling rests on — trace distance, booked optimal, charged total, the pattern counters — sits on an artifact at weight_multiplier 1.0. The MISSING advisory carries no fact; the finding survives its absence at weight 0.0 and is named here for the record.

OUTCOME: FULL_REFUND, SGD 62.28 to the rider.

ruling.explanation: The route-deviation claim is made out. All three load-bearing artifacts — trip record EV-TRIP-00515, GPS trace EV-GPS-00515 and fare breakdown EV-FARE-00515 — carry trip_id TRP-00515 and cohere in time (accepted 17:30:40, started/first fix 17:36:40, ended/last fix 18:37:40), so the rider's threshold burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged. On the governing distance figure — the trace, trace_distance_km 48.82 km, which POL-RD-01 makes govern over the rounded trip-record copy of 48.8 km — the excess over the 34.2 km booked optimal is 14.62 km, or 42.75%. That passes both POL-RD-01 establishment limbs (20% of 34.2 km = 6.84 km; absolute floor 0.8 km) and also exceeds the 8.0 km materiality threshold, so this is a MATERIAL deviation. The driver's point that the raw measurement does not, by itself, support a claim to the whole fare is correct and is the starting point of the arithmetic below; it is not the end of the case. The trace is clean for policy purposes: 367 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, so POL-RD-07(a)–(c) is not engaged and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises. The driver's accusation of slow driving is not supported by the trace either (sustained speeds of 45–50 kph), but that cuts against the conduct narrative only, not the route finding. No exculpatory clause runs. The driver's statement blames a confusing KPE split and admits he missed it once — an admission of driver error, not an external traffic cause — and in any event the bundle holds no traffic advisory: EV-ADVIS-00515-01 is MISSING at weight_multiplier 0.0 (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). Under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 that assertion is tested against the advisory and carries no weight, and POL-RD-03 is unavailable. Because the driver named no advisory evidence ID, POL-RD-13(1) applies and the missing advisory is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. POL-RD-04 is unavailable: the single chat message (17:48:40, 'can you please put the phone down and drive') has waypoint_hint null and names no road or place. POL-RD-05 does not run (no amendment timestamps). POL-RD-12 does not apply (vehicle_type RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL), so the 34.2 km booked optimal is the correct baseline. The POL-RD-02 arithmetic, on its own line: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 × 34.2 + 0.28 × 40.0) × surge 1.0 (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP on the optimal route = 41.45; refund = charged_total 62.28 − 41.45 = 20.83, rounded UP to SGD 20.85. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply, and the meter was not inflated (48.8 km billed against 48.82 km traced; 61.0 min billed against the record), so there is no billing-integrity defect and no POL-RD-09(4) referral. The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is required by the MATERIAL finding, and a repeat deviation pattern is established: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3, meeting the clause's '3 or more' limb, against 180 completed trips in the window. The driver is right that the trailing-window rate (3/180 = 1.67%) is below the clause's 5% limb and that prior_deviation_flags (5) is a lifetime counter POL-GEN-01 makes context-only and inadmissible for this test — but the clause is disjunctive and the count limb alone establishes the pattern, so the driver's narrower reading does not defeat it. Under POL-RD-06(b) the remedy is uplifted from the POL-RD-02 partial to FULL_REFUND of the charged total. Stated side by side as the clause requires: POL-RD-02 standing alone yields SGD 20.85; the uplifted figure is the charged_total of SGD 62.28, of which SGD 58.28 (distance, time and platform charges) is uplifted by this limb and SGD 4.00 of off-route ERP is settled under POL-RD-09 rather than uplifted. Both charged gantries (TPE Seletar Link, SGD 2.00; TPE Punggol Rd, SGD 2.00) are matched to trace fixes at 0 m and carry on_optimal_route = false; they are itemised for transparency and are comprehended in the award, never added on top a second time. The conduct complaints (phone use, hard braking, lane drift) are not priced by any fare line and do not change the money; they are answered through the POL-RD-06(c) referral below, which the established pattern produces and which does not displace or delay this monetary ruling. The counterparty statement carries no weight_multiplier and so enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of the POL-GEN-02(2) cap; it is evidence, and its admissions of phone use and of missing the split are noted, but they carry no fare consequence. All facts this ruling rests on are carried by artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0 (trace, trip record, fare breakdown, driver profile), so the cap is 1.0 and confidence is set at 0.85.

The rider's threshold case under POL-RD-08(a) is therefore made out, and the booked optimal route on the trip record is 34.2 km and 40.0 minutes.

The governing distance is the trace figure, not the rounded trip-record copy. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km (48.82 km) govern where it disagrees with trip_record.actual_distance_km (48.8 km), and the trip-record field may not be cited for the threshold test. Measured on the governing figure against the 34.2 km optimal, the excess is 14.62 km.

The deviation is established on both limbs of POL-RD-01: an excess of 14.62 km is more than 20% of the 34.2 km optimal (the 20% line is 6.84 km) and more than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The trace reports the excess as 42.75% of optimal.
The deviation is additionally MATERIAL: an excess of 14.62 km exceeds the 8.0 km absolute materiality threshold set out in POL-RD-01, which in turn requires the driver_profile check under POL-RD-06.

The trace is clean for policy purposes. It carries 367 fixes at a 10 s interval against an expected 10 s, no gaps at all, max_gap_sec 0.0 and 100% coverage. It meets none of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07, so no impairment discount applies, the measured excess is the excess, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is engaged.

The driver has no admissible exculpation. His statement blames a confusing KPE split and an admission that he missed it, but he cites no advisory. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00515-01, is MISSING: status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. POL-RD-03 cannot be run without a named corridor and validity window, and under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 the assertion carries no weight; the measured excess therefore stands unreduced.

There was no rider-requested detour. The chat log holds exactly one message, the rider asking the driver to put the phone down, with waypoint_hint null and no road or place named. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction that identifies a waypoint or road and is corroborated by the vehicle passing within 200 m of it; neither exists here, so the clause is unavailable to the driver and no part of the excess is excluded.

The optimal baseline is the booked optimal of 34.2 km. This trip is RYDE_PLUS, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline and its co-rider exclusion do not apply and cannot be used to explain any part of the 14.62 km excess away.

A repeat deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3, which meets the clause's threshold of 3 or more, against 180 completed trips in the same window (well above the 40-trip floor). Under POL-GEN-01 the claim rests on those two named fields only and on no other profile field.

Because the POL-RD-06 pattern is established, and because this deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own trace, limb (b) uplifts the remedy from the POL-RD-02 partial to FULL_REFUND of charged_total. The two figures printed side by side, as the clause requires: POL-RD-02 standing alone yields SGD 20.85 (charged_total 62.28 less recomputed_fare 41.45, rounded up); the uplifted outcome is the entire charged_total of SGD 62.28 — SGD 58.28 of distance, time and platform charges uplifted by this limb, plus the SGD 4.00 of off-route ERP which POL-RD-09 settles on its own footing and which this limb does not need to uplift.

If the uplift is declined, the ordinary POL-RD-02 arithmetic still runs: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 34.2 + 0.28 x 40.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP on the optimal route = 41.45; refund = 62.28 - 41.45 = 20.83, rounded up to SGD 20.85 payable. The fare_model is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE, so POL-RD-02 and not POL-RD-11 governs, and the surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is 1.0.

The SGD 4.00 of ERP is wholly off-route: both charged gantries, TPE (Seletar Link towards Punggol) and TPE (Punggol Rd towards Tampines), carry on_optimal_route = false, and each is matched to a trace fix at 0 m. Under POL-RD-09 these pass-through lines travel with the deviation refund, are itemised separately in the ruling, and are never added on top of the distance-and-time figure a second time.

The rider's account is corroborated beyond the trace, so the case is not a trace-only case. At 17:48:40, twelve minutes into the trip, the rider messaged 'can you please put the phone down and drive', and the driver's own counter-statement concedes 'I was checking the navigation on my phone'. That combination supports the POL-RD-06(c) referral to driver-conduct review, which is recorded in the ruling's referrals list and does not displace or delay the monetary outcome.

The rider carries no adverse claim history that would add a corroboration burden. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 rider-side trigger (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) does not fire, and the ordinary burden is discharged on this trip's own trace. Under POL-GEN-01 no other rider profile field bears on the outcome.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance figure is the trace, gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 48.82 km, not the rounded trip_record convenience copy of 48.8 km. Measured against the 34.2 km booked optimal, the excess is 14.62 km, or 42.75 percent. That is the whole of the departure the rider can point to: 34.2 of the 48.8 km driven was the optimal route, so a claim to the entire 62.28 SGD fare is not supported by this trip's own measurement.

The rider's account of a driver 'driving slowly so he could keep scrolling' is contradicted by the driver's own trace: 367 fixes at a 10 s cadence record sustained speeds clustered in the 45-50 kph band with a single low reading of 4.4 kph, and the trace carries no hard-braking or lane-drift signature at all. The narrative, not the data, is doing the work in that part of the claim.

The trip ran 61 minutes against a 40-minute optimal - 21 minutes over, not the 'forty minutes became ninety' of the claim - and the only in-app message on the trip is the rider's own, sent at 17:48:40. Under POL-RD-02 the recomputation runs on optimal_duration_min = 40.0 against the recording engine's duration, not against the rider's account of the journey.

The substance of the claim - phone use, two hard brakes, lane drift and the rider's fear - is a conduct complaint. No line of the fare_breakdown prices conduct, and the route-deviation policy's only monetary remedy is the arithmetic recomputation in POL-RD-02. Under POL-GEN-03 the ruling moves the figure that arithmetic produces for a route deviation and nothing more; conduct is a referral matter, not a fare line.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 367 fixes at a 10 s cadence, 100 percent coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is therefore not engaged, the trace is not impaired for policy purposes, and there is no POL-RD-10(3) escalation available on this bundle.

The 4.00 SGD of off-route ERP is already comprehended in the fare refund under POL-RD-09(1) and must never be added on top of it. The driver's exposure on this trip is one figure, not a sum made of a distance refund plus the gantry lines itemised a second time.

The meter was not inflated. The distance charged, 48.8 km, matches the 48.82 km the trace records, and the time charged, 61.0 minutes, matches the trip record; the fare model on this trip is METERED, so the billed lines are the trace lines. The driver billed no more distance or time than the trace shows he drove, so the rider is not paying for padded meter movement.

Any POL-RD-06 pattern finding must rest on driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d alone: POL-GEN-01 makes prior_deviation_flags - 5 on this profile - a lifetime counter that is context only and cannot be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure the clause names, and the trailing-window rate here is 3 of 180 trips, 1.67 percent, far below the clause's 5 percent limb.
